To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the γδ TCR is critical for the development of epidermal γ/δ T cells and that allelic exclusion does not operate on TCR-δ genes.

TCR-δ chain expression is not sufficient for the development of epidermal γ6δ3+ T cells, but that TCR-αβ+ thymocytes expressing a TCR-α chain specific for the same antigen as the γ6δ3 chain are required for the development and/or migration of these cells to the epidermis.
TCR specificity and the TCR-γ/δ locus are required for the development and/or localization of epidermal γ/δ T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of γ/δ T lymphocytes, a T cell population which is characterized by a restricted TCR usage.
the role of TCR specificity in the development of epidermal γ6δ T cells and the mechanisms underlying this process.
the role of TCR specificity in γδ T cell migration/localization to epithelial tissues and with the mechanisms of allelic exclusion of TCR-δ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TCR specificity and the presence of endogenous Vδ1 transcripts are required for the development and/or maintenance of γδ T lymphocytes in the epidermal compartment.
the expression of a TCR-δ chain in DETC development is required, but not sufficient.
the TCR specificity is required for the migration of Vγ3+ γδ T cells to the skin, whereas the presence of an endogenous Vδ1 TCR-δ chain in DETC may be required for their development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
γδ T cells expressing Vγ3/Vγ8.3/Vδ6.3 TCRs are not restricted to the epidermis but can be found in other lymphoid tissues.
TCR specificity determines the tissue distribution of γδ T lymphocytes.
TCR specificity and TCR-δ expression are both required for γδ T cell development in the epidermal microenvironment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TCR specificity, rather than the TCR itself, is critical for the migration/localization of γδ T lymphocytes in the skin.

γδ T cell development in the thymus is a two-step process, in which the first step is the selection of γδ T lymphocytes with a particular specificity, while the second is the selection of cells that express the correct Vγ and Vδ segments.
TCR specificity determines γδ T cell development and migration/localization.
